articles.title: Den gør mange menneskers liv bedre – og andres værre: Nu overvejer Norge et forbud
articles.summary: Udsatte grupper i vores samfund nyder stor gavn af AI, så vores frygt kan risikere at gå ud over dem, mener forskere.
articles.why: Norske politikere overvejer et forbud mod en form for AI-teknologi efter forskere påpeger, at systemet hjælper udsatte grupper men samtidig skader andre. Det ændrer debatten om regulering i Norden; Mads bør kende konsekvenserne for dansk policy- og velfærdstale.

articles.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
articles.summary: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law,…
articles.why: Forskere præsenterer 'reverse game theory' som en praktisk metode til at designe incitamenter, så autonome AI-agenter overholder regler. Teksten er relevant for danske beslutningstagere og forsvars- eller sikkerhedsdiskussioner om agent-sikkerhed.

articles.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
articles.summary: Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.
articles.why: Anthropic udvikler 'FlashProve' til at verificere, at et svar virkelig kommer fra den påståede model — et vigtigt skridt mod ansvarlig AI-udrulning og provenance, som påvirker danske virksomheder og myndigheders tillid til AI-tjenester.

articles.title: CrowdStrike to shell out nearly $500M for 2 AI security startups as the market for securing agents takes off | TechCrunch
articles.summary: CrowdStrike said it will buy Fiddler AI, which makes AI agent observability software, and Dreadnode, which helps companies automate AI security testing.
articles.why: CrowdStrike køber to AI-sikkerhedsstartups for ~$500M—et tydeligt signal om, at markedet for at sikre AI-agenter og deres output er splinterny og kapitaltung. Dette har implikationer for virksomheder og danske it-sikkerhedsstrategier.

articles.title: Nearly all Americans believe corruption is a problem. But will it decide the midterm elections?
articles.summary: The vast majority of Americans believe government corruption is widespread – both Democrats and Republicans. Politicians have taken notice. Share article Print article In a politically polarised American electorate, it can be hard to find bipartisan consensus on many issues. Ahead of the US midterm elections, however, there is one thing almost everyone can agree on: concern about government corruption.
articles.why: Længere gennemgang af korruptionsbekymringens rolle i amerikansk politik før midtvejsvalget. God baggrund for at forstå amerikanske politiske strømninger, som kan påvirke håndteringen af transatlantiske spørgsmål relevant for Danmark.

articles.title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?
articles.summary: Graduates are spending more time managing AI, but are they missing out on other work experience? Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR. Underwood, 25, joined London-based PR agency Fight or Flight in November last year, in the new role of "AI associate" after completing a degree and then a masters in marketing.
articles.why: Undersøger hvordan nye dimittender primært arbejder som AI-managers og mister bredere læringserfaringer — relevant for dansk arbejdsmarked, uddannelsespolitik og diskussionen om fremtidens kompetencer.
